hypothesis: This is the reference arm of a second-seed width-scaling test. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=256, best-of-3 controls, seed 23, N=64, 6000 steps. Prediction: N=64 force is saturated in width. Final trained force R2 at the best-margin layer stays within 0.03 of this seed's d_model=128 N=64 value of 0.81015 (layer 1, run-20261016-002356-c1d5), and force beats its control. If so, any change with width in the N=64 minus N=128 gap comes from the N=128 side. All values come from probes_final, unrounded, with the layer reported, and layer-1 force R2 is reported separately. The gap against the paired d_model=256 N=128 arm uses best-margin layers, with cross-layer pairs flagged, plus a layer-1 same-layer gap wherever both arms list layer 1. Both arms' run IDs are cited. If the paired arm is unavailable, the gap is reported as not computed. Comparisons use trained R2, not margin. No band is placed on control R2.
expected_if_true: Best-margin-layer N=64 force R2 is in [0.78, 0.84], the force margin is >= required_margin, and the N=64 values serve as the reference for the paired gap.
expected_if_false: N=64 force R2 is > 0.84, so N=64 also gains from width (the gap then depends on both arms), or < 0.78, so wider models lose N=64 force decodability. Either result means N=64 is not width-saturated, and any change in the gap cannot be put down to the N=128 side alone.
